title: Choose the Smallest Slice That Can Change the Decision
service: SlicePick: proof-first reversible experiments and decision records
runtime: Python3.10+, standard library and pytest; no model/network

parts.lesson_anchor: Define Required Proof First; score consequence and reversibility; decision alternatives
planted_bugs: zero effort accepted then division fails inside score
reversible consequence coefficients reversed in score; choose consumes wrong score and selects wrong id one layer away
equal-content candidate alternatives lost by value filtering
each required proof linearly rescans offered tuple
parts.overfix_guard: nonempty-proof and numeric-type helpers supplied correct; raw offered evidence preserved

parts.lesson_anchor: Keep outputs/slice-decision.json with why this slice is smallest useful evidence
parts.storage: atomic JSON complete typed decision snapshot using provided replacement helper
parts.exactness: candidate identity, nested dataclasses/tuples, raw proofs/stop rules, bool and exact float including negative zero
traps: invalid selected id rejected before writing

parts.lesson_anchor: Common False Minimums; Add a Stop Rule
parts.algorithm: relative ProofNeed audit of all false-minimum fields then eligible score selection
traps: proof eligibility and effective stop rule before scoring
three explicit actions at least one changes keep-building

parts.lesson_anchor: Add a Stop Rule before implementation
parts.wire_format: SSE measurement/decision using provided JSON data serializer
traps: terminal and cancellation do not pull future inputs

parts.lesson_anchor: Vertical Means Evidence End to End
traps: minimum unbuilt nodes not total length
connected trigger to first outcome including endpoints

deviations: Candidate stable ids preserve source Slice value equality while distinguishing decision alternatives. The source score coefficients are retained; 49 supplies its correct risk formula so these lessons do not both repair risk-formula signs.
Required-proof nonemptiness/normalization and numeric type guards are supplied correct. The empty-proof boundary remains a guard rather than another planted vacuous-truth defect.
Part2 enriches source JSON with typed Snapshot and StopRule. Correct single-writer atomic replacement is supplied, not a repeated candidate commit/rename task.
False minimums use explicit Design/ProofNeed fields, not inferred natural language. UI comprehension remains legitimate when real-data proof is not required.

A controlled pilot uses explicit consecutive-error limit and EOF actions; this exercises a stop rule without claiming those outcomes establish statistical experiment success. SSE encoding is supplied correct.
The finite workflow DAG and minimum unbuilt-node cost are an exercise representation of a vertical evidence chain. Source does not teach a general graph optimizer; DAG validation is supplied.
